screen_device.what_it_is: crude cross-sectional rank book built directly on the pinned RAW y4 matrix: eligible = member AND finite y4 AND qv4h>=2.5e5 (the live gate, shadow_loop_v3 L473-474); weights = centred cross-sectional rank, normalised to sum|w|=1; per-anchor gross = 1e4 * sum(w*y4); turnover = sum|w_t - w_{t-1}|

single_most_important_reading: There IS a large, genuinely near-orthogonal gross alpha on data we already hold: short-horizon cross-sectional reversal pays 1.1585 bps/anchor of gross -- 87% of the ENTIRE live book's gross alpha (A0 pnl_ex 1.3266) -- at rho +0.0189 to A0. It is not admissible because its break-even is 0.88 bps per unit turnover (1.60 after the book's own EMA shaping) against every execution rate we have evidence for (2.95 / 3.78 / 5.53 / 13.2), AND because it vanishes in the liquid tier (tier0 gross -0.0963) where cost is cheapest. Those two facts together identify it as the bid-ask/liquidity premium rather than a forecast. That does not close it -- it relocates it: the object is not a signal to be traded through, it is a spread to be quoted.
